name: Melanocytic Nevus (Common Mole)
description: A common mole is a harmless, non-cancerous skin spot made of pigment-producing cells. Most people have between 10 and 40 moles on their body, which usually appear during childhood and young adulthood.
common_symptoms: Small round or oval spot with smooth, even borders
Single even color across the entire spot, usually pink, tan, or brown
Can be flat or slightly raised above the skin
Usually smaller than 6 mm across (pencil eraser size)
Remains stable and does not change rapidly over time
causes: Normal clusters of pigment cells (melanocytes) growing together in the skin
first_aid: Normal stable moles do not need any medical treatment
If accidentally cut or nicked while shaving, clean gently with soap and water and apply a clean bandage
Take a baseline photo to keep track of its appearance over time
precautions: Protect moles from sunburn with SPF 30+ sunscreen
Check your moles once a month to ensure they remain stable
Avoid scratching or rubbing elevated moles with rough jewelry or belts
home_care: Wash skin gently with mild soap and water
Leave stable moles alone without picking
do_not: DO NOT try to cut, scrape, slice, or burn off a mole yourself
DO NOT apply strong acids or homemade chemicals to remove a mole
DO NOT ignore a mole if it starts growing, itching, or bleeding
red_flags: A mole that begins growing larger rapidly
A mole that develops jagged or fuzzy edges
A mole that turns black or has more than two different colors
A mole that starts bleeding, crusting, or oozing without being scratched
when_to_see_doctor: See a doctor if an existing mole changes in size, shape, or color, or if a new mole looks unusual compared to your other spots.
prevention: Protect skin from strong sun exposure
Wear protective clothing and hats outdoors
